web:ti-slvs841g-tps2553.title: TPS255xx Precision Adjustable Current-Limited Power-Distribution Switches, SLVS841G (November 2008, revised October 2026)
web:ti-slvs841g-tps2553.note: Also covers TPS2553DBVR (constant-current). p.1: constant-current (TPS255x) and latch-off (TPS255x-1) versions, 2.5-6.5 V, 85 mOhm (DBV). p.4 (Figure 5-1, DBV pinout 1 IN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 ILIM, 5 FAULT, 6 OUT; EN active high for TPS2553): "Add -1 to part number for latch-off version". p.14 note A: TPS255x parts go to constant current in current limit, TPS255x-1 parts latch off; the -1 latches off after the internal deglitch time (7.5 ms typical) and stays off until power is cycled or the device enable is toggled. p.15 (8.3.3): TPS255x asserts FAULT until the fault is removed; TPS255x-1 keeps FAULT asserted while latched off, and FAULT de-asserts once device power is cycled or the enable is toggled; TPS255x thermal-cycles (off above TJ 135 C min, restart after about 10 C cooling). p.16 (8.5.1): recommended RILIM 15k-232k (1 %). pp.16-17 eq. (1)-(3), RILIM in kOhm: IOSmax(mA) = 22980/RILIM^0.94, IOSnom = 23950/RILIM^0.977, IOSmin = 25230/RILIM^1.016 (resistor tolerance not included). Arithmetic from these equations (not a datasheet table): RILIM 162k gives 143.6 / 166.2 / 192.5 mA (min/nom/max); 88.7k gives 264.7 / 299.4 / 339.1 mA. p.29 package option addendum: TPS2553DBVR and TPS2553DBVR-1 both Active, SOT-23 (DBV) 6, 3000 large T&R, NIPDAU, MSL 1-260C-UNLIM, -40 to 125 C; marking 2553 (TPS2553DBVR) and CHZ (TPS2553DBVR-1). web:quectel-lc76g-hd-v1-3.method: curl (default User-Agent), text via PyMuPDF (owner-encrypted PDF, text readable); page numbers below are the document footer numbers (PDF page = footer + 1)
web:quectel-lc76g-hd-v1-3.title: LC76G Series Hardware Design V1.3 (2024-11-25)
web:quectel-lc76g-hd-v1-3.note: Supply current (VCC typ. 3.3 V for LC76G (AB)/(PA), 2.55-3.6 V, Table 12 p.42; (PB) 1.75-1.98 V): Table 14 pp.44-45 IVCC typ. with GPS+GLONASS+Galileo+BDS+QZSS acquisition 33 mA (AB) / 9.7 mA (PA) / 15.6 mA (PB), tracking 32.9 / 9.7 / 15.6 mA; IPEAK 58 / 24 / 36 mA (footnote 5: used to determine maximum current capability of the power supply; transient pulse currents at power-up and mode transitions excluded); IV_BCKP 130 / 127 / 122 uA, Backup mode 13 uA. Table 3 p.14 repeats the acquisition/tracking values. p.25 (3.2.1): TVS plus 10 uF, 100 nF and 33 pF near VCC; a switching DC-DC converter is not recommended. UART while VCC is off: the document has no explicit back-power or I/O-leakage statement (searched for back, leakage, powered off). What it does state: IO_Domain = VCC and VIH max = VCC + 0.3 V (Table 12 p.42, recommended operating conditions); VIN_IO absolute maximum -0.3 to 3.63 V (Table 10 p.41) and "the product is not protected against over-voltage or reversed voltage" (p.42); Figures 9 and 10 (pp.29-30) show UART valid only while VCC is valid; V_BCKP must be powered simultaneously with VCC or before it (3.4 p.29); power-on restart by lowering VCC and V_BCKP below 100 mV for at least 1 s (3.5 p.30); p.32: if the MCU I/O voltage does not match the module, a level-shifting circuit must be used. So a high level driven into RXD while VCC is 0 V is outside the recommended VIH range (above VCC + 0.3 V) but not addressed by any rule beyond that. Which LC76G variant the Waveshare 24370 board carries is not shown in this document.
